questions.q: Juan Nakpil was the first architect to be conferred which prestigious title by the Philippine government in 1973?
questions.n: Nakpil was the pioneer recipient of this honor, recognizing his immense influence on the country's built environment.

questions.q: Nakpil is famously credited with the 1930s reconstruction and expansion of which iconic church in Manila, known for its Black Nazarene?
questions.n: Nakpil added the dome and a second bell tower, giving the church its current iconic Baroque-inspired silhouette.

questions.q: Which prominent administrative building in UP Diliman, featuring a grand overhead gateway and the Oblation statue, was designed by Juan Nakpil?
questions.n: As the gateway to the university, Quezon Hall is one of Nakpil's most recognizable neoclassical-modernist hybrids.

questions.q: The Manila Jockey Club (San Lazaro Hippodrome), designed by Nakpil, was a premier example of which architectural style popular in the 1930s?
questions.n: Nakpil utilized Art Deco's geometric patterns and streamlined forms to give the Jockey Club a modern, high-speed aesthetic.

questions.q: Aside from his buildings, Juan Nakpil was also a renowned designer of furniture. Which famous Filipino historical house did he help restore and furnish?
questions.n: Nakpil was commissioned to reconstruct the Rizal home to its original 19th-century appearance based on historical research.

questions.q: Nakpil's design for the Rizal Theater in Makati (now replaced) was famous for its excellent acoustics. What was his primary focus when designing theaters?
o: The integration of sound, sightlines, and structural efficiency
Building the tallest tower in the city
questions.n: Nakpil was known for his technical precision in ensuring that every seat had a clear view and perfect sound quality.

questions.q: Which building at the University of the Philippines did Nakpil design to look like an open book?
questions.n: This building is one of his most celebrated works on campus, symbolizing the storage and dissemination of knowledge.

questions.q: True or False: Juan Nakpil was the son of Julio Nakpil, a composer and general of the Philippine Revolution, and Gregoria de Jesus, the 'Lakambini of the Katipunan.'
questions.n: His lineage connected him deeply to the history of the Philippine struggle for independence, which influenced his nationalist architectural spirit.

questions.q: Nakpil's 'Ever Theater' on Manila's Rizal Avenue was a landmark of which era of urban development?
o: The Post-War Golden Age of Cinema
questions.n: This theater was part of the vibrant commercial and entertainment boom in downtown Manila during the mid-20th century.

questions.q: Juan Nakpil was a key figure in the creation of the first professional organization for architects in the Philippines. What is this organization?
questions.n: Nakpil was a founding member and a past president of the Philippine Institute of Architects (PIA), which later merged into the UAP.

questions.q: Juan Nakpil's design for the Geronimo de los Reyes Building showcased a shift in his style. Which architectural movement did this building represent in the context of 1930s Manila?
questions.n: This building featured the streamlined, geometric ornamentation and verticality characteristic of the Art Deco era in the Philippines.

questions.q: In his mission to create a 'Filipino Architecture,' what was Nakpil's primary stance on the use of local materials like wood and stone?
o: They were only suitable for small residential huts
They should be replaced entirely by imported steel and glass
They should be integrated with modern technology to suit the Philippine climate
They should be used exclusively to avoid any Western influence
questions.n: Nakpil believed that architecture must be functional for the tropics, utilizing local materials where they improved comfort and identity.

questions.q: The UP Main Library (Gonzalez Hall) is noted for its 'open book' profile. Aside from this, what functional feature did Nakpil emphasize in its design?
o: An underground storage system to avoid floods
A flat roof designed for social gatherings
A completely windowless facade for security
questions.n: Nakpil was a master of passive cooling, ensuring that the library remained comfortable despite the Philippine heat.

questions.q: Juan Nakpil was commissioned to reconstruct the Rizal House in Calamba. Which architectural 'rule' did he strictly follow for this project?
questions.n: Nakpil performed extensive research to ensure the house looked exactly as it did during Jose Rizal's childhood, down to the materials used.

questions.q: Nakpil's design for the Social Security System (SSS) Building in Quezon City reflects which later phase of his career?
questions.n: The SSS building features the clean lines, sun-shading devices (brise-soleil), and functionalism of the 1960s.

questions.q: True or False: Juan Nakpil was also a skilled civil engineer, which allowed him to personally calculate the structural integrity of his complex Art Deco designs.
questions.n: His background in engineering was crucial for executing the innovative spans and cantilevered sections of buildings like the Manila Jockey Club.

questions.q: The 'Nakpil-Bautista House' in Quiapo is a family heritage. What was Nakpil's role regarding this 19th-century structure?
o: He designed its original structure in the 1800s
He demolished it to build a modern office
He renovated and preserved its Viennese Secession-inspired details
He converted it into a purely Art Deco building
questions.n: Growing up in this house influenced his appreciation for European styles integrated into Filipino homes.

questions.q: Which of these theaters designed by Nakpil was famous for its sweeping, curved facade and served as a cultural hub on Avenida Rizal?
questions.n: The Ever was one of his most prominent theater designs, showcasing the 'Streamline Moderne' influence of late Art Deco.

questions.q: Juan Nakpil designed several residences for Manila's elite. Which element was a signature of his residential 'Filipino Modern' style?
o: Wide eaves and open plans for air circulation
Using only heavy stone for all interior walls
Small windows to mimic European castles
Excluding gardens to maximize floor area
questions.n: He adapted the principles of the Bahay Kubo—elevation, shade, and airflow—into modern, luxurious residential designs.

questions.q: The 'Magsaysay Center' on Roxas Boulevard was a collaboration between Nakpil's firm and which international architectural entity?
questions.n: This firm collaborated with Nakpil to produce a building that was a marvel of pre-stressed concrete and glass.

questions.q: The Magsaysay Center on Roxas Boulevard is a landmark of structural engineering. What unique material property did Nakpil and his collaborators use to allow for its slender, resilient frame?
questions.n: This technique allowed the building to have thinner slabs and greater structural strength against earthquakes and wind.

questions.q: When Nakpil redesigned the Quiapo Church dome, he moved away from the traditional Spanish style. What was his primary architectural goal for the new silhouette?
o: To make it look like a modern glass pyramid
To reduce the height so it wouldn't be seen from the street
To use only lightweight plastic materials for the dome
To create a more balanced, Baroque-inspired massing with twin bell towers
questions.n: Nakpil's intervention gave the church the grand, symmetrical presence it is known for today, enhancing its visual importance in the district.

questions.q: Juan Nakpil often criticized 'Western' skyscrapers for being 'ovens.' What was his specific architectural solution to prevent this in his Philippine designs?
o: The use of 'brise-soleil' and wide eaves to provide shade
Removing all windows to keep out the sun
Painting every building entirely black to absorb heat
questions.n: By incorporating sun-shading devices, he reduced heat gain while allowing for natural light and air.

questions.q: In his residential works, Nakpil often utilized a 'split-level' floor plan. What was the functional benefit of this in a tropical setting?
o: It was designed to prevent the family from seeing each other
It was purely a decorative trend with no functional purpose
It encouraged the natural flow of air through the house
It was a requirement for all houses in Makati
questions.n: Varying floor heights helped create pressure differences that moved air more efficiently than a single flat floor.

questions.q: Which of these institutions did Juan Nakpil help found to ensure that architects were properly trained and licensed in the Philippines?
o: The Department of Environment and Natural Resources
questions.n: Nakpil was a cornerstone of the PIA, which was the first professional organization for architects in the country.
